Yes. 

Throughout the dialogue, the tension builds between Markus and Jonas, culminating in Jonas abruptly standing up to leave when Markus brings up a painful memory ("der Sommer am See"). Because Jonas has been defensive, distant, and avoidant the entire time—even complaining about the coffee he hasn't tasted just to have an excuse to leave—the reader expects him to walk out for good. 

However, his sudden turn at the door to ask, "Nächste Woche. Dienstag?" (Next week. Tuesday?) is **surprising** because it subverts the expectation of a final, bitter departure. At the same time, it is entirely **appropriate** within the context of their established relationship. Earlier in the conversation, they established a twenty-year history of drinking bad coffee together out of "Gewohnheit" (habit) and an unspoken, lingering care for one another (Jonas offering updates on the shop, his mother asking about Markus). Thus, Jonas's inability to fully sever ties, masked behind a gruff, habitual routine, makes complete sense for his character.
